title: Quiescent fleet exercise and fallback-candidate verification
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Purpose: Run automated exercises against passive (quiescent) regional fleets to validate that fallback candidate model variants and passive cache state meet cutover requirements before an operational region failover. The goal is to provide a deterministic, observable readiness score per region so smart routing can promote a standby region with confidence and automated rollback heuristics.

Scope:
- Validate prefix/KV cache 'warmth' for common customer prefixes and model shards.
- Verify model-variant compatibility matrix (float16 => quantized INT8/4 variants) under production sequence length distributions.
- Ensure tokenizer & decode parity across model variants (byte-level invariants and whitespace/detokenization checks).
- Execute staged canary traffic injection to exercise tail-latency SLOs without affecting live traffic.
- Confirm kernel compatibility (chosen backend kernels, fused attention availability) and GPU memory reservation behavior for each variant.
- Run deterministic fallbacks: capacity-aware policy simulation to pick the optimal model variant and region tier on overload.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Each region reports a readiness_score >= 0.87 for the set of 500 representative prefixes and 25 synthetic long-tail prompts. Score components: cache_warmth, kv_match_rate, latency_tail, tokenization_parity, kernel_ok_rate.
2) For each candidate fallback variant we have a certified compatibility tag and a populated rollback-playbook with automated routing adjustments.
3) Canary traffic experiment finishes with no user-facing errors and meets 99th percentile latency SLO for that variant under simulated 20% burst.
4) Observability dashboards show per-token cost delta, cache hit-rate, and top-5 failure modes for variant transitions.

Implementation notes:
- New "exercise-runner" job will be scheduled in the orchestrator: sequence = cache-probe -> model-load-check -> tokenization-sanity -> lite-bench (90s) -> canary-inject (3m) -> post-checks.
- Cache probe: compute deterministic KV checksum for selected prefixes and compare against golden snapshot sampled from primary region. Allow for acceptable staleness window (configurable).
- Model-load-check: attempt loading candidate quantized variants on a fenced GPU node with memory reservation to detect OOM/placement differences.
- Canary-inject: route synthetic requests through the same smart-routing path but tag them for no billing and telemetry-only tracing.
- Readiness score formula and thresholds are configurable via configmap in ops repo and surfaced as a Console widget.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: checksum false-negatives due to minor cache eviction timing. Mitigation: use rolling-window histograms and allow small delta tolerance per-token.
- Risk: synthetic canary may not reproduce real end-to-end networking artifacts. Mitigation: include a subset of flagged customer prefixes that consented to diagnostics.
- Risk: long-run GPU reservation could reduce capacity. Mitigation: limit exercises to off-peak windows and have a strict concurrency cap.

Artifacts: Confluence runbook and playbook, design doc, and prototype PRs are listed below in links.

Operational playbook stub (to be expanded):
- If readiness_score < threshold: mark region as quarantine and increment backoff timer for subsequent exercises.
- If canary fails with OOM or kernel mismatch: automatically nominate next fallback variant and run variant-compat check.
- If canary passes but latency degrades >20%: rollback routing to primary region and create incident with exec summary.
